# Inspiration Sources

Use these publisher pages and labeled research sources for product, business, community, design, and engineering questions.

Read **Design Standards and Product Context** for principles, **Background Reading** for origins, adoption, and past use, **App Inspirations** for product or technical research, and **Visual References** when you need images.

## Design Standards and Product Context

| Reference | Sources and Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Apple | [Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/), [developer documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/). Use these as the leading human-centered design standard for clarity, control, presentation, and ease of use. |
| Google and Android | [Google Design](https://design.google/), [Android design guidance](https://developer.android.com/design), [app development guidance](https://developer.android.com/guide), [app quality](https://developer.android.com/quality). Use these as the other main design standard, including Android behavior and integration. This doesn't mandate [Material Design](https://material.io/) as the visual style. |
| Third places | [Third-place concept](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_place). Understand the social purpose behind discovery. |
| React Native | [Documentation](https://reactnative.dev/docs/getting-started), [performance](https://reactnative.dev/docs/performance), [source](https://github.com/facebook/react-native) for native implementation guidance. |
| Expo | [Documentation](https://docs.expo.dev/), [documentation index](https://docs.expo.dev/llms.txt), [source](https://github.com/expo/expo). Discover the relevant supported APIs and examples. |

## Background Reading

These linked accounts and summaries provide established context, not a live feature list or a complete history of every app. Read the relevant account when you need more detail.

### Beli's Origins and Product Lessons

In their [Founder Brew interview](https://www.founderbrew.com/stories/beli-founders-judy-thelen-eliot-frost-partnership-superpower), Beli's founders describe starting with a shared, ranked restaurant map containing notes and favorite dishes. They describe testing demand through social media beyond their small friends-and-classmates beta, and warn that friends may not provide representative feedback. They also explain why real-world activity, rather than time spent in the app, should guide their product's success measures. This is exactly the same heart that Charlotte Third Places has. The goal is that people use the app to leave the app, as in find a place, a physical real life place, to spend time, hang out, meet friends, make friends, and all things in between.

### Beli's Adoption and Recorded Use

A [TASTE report with user and founder interviews](https://tastecooking.com/beli-invites-the-loneliest-generation-to-dine-out/) documents adoption through friend networks and local dining communities. Users describe keeping restaurant lists and food journals, sharing reviews and photos, and using friends' recommendations to choose outings. The report also records concerns about comparing unlike places and amplifying hype. These accounts illustrate benefits and trade-offs, not proof of what caused growth. Charlotte Third Places wants to emulate this success.

## App Inspirations

Choose references from the full catalog by relevance, not by their order in this table. Pinterest, Google Maps, Beli, and AllTrails are especially relevant, not exclusive.

| App | Publisher and Research Sources |
| --- | --- |
| Pinterest | [Gestalt design system](https://gestalt.pinterest.systems/), [Engineering](https://medium.com/pinterest-engineering), [Gestalt source](https://github.com/pinterest/gestalt), [public repositories](https://github.com/pinterest) for visual discovery, interaction patterns, and performance research. |
| Google Maps | [Product help](https://support.google.com/maps/), [Local Guides points, levels, and badges](https://support.google.com/local-guides/answer/6225851), [contribution policies](https://support.google.com/contributionpolicy/answer/7400114), [Maps Platform documentation](https://developers.google.com/maps/), [public examples](https://github.com/googlemaps). Study maps, discovery, contributor profiles, community participation, reputation, recognition, and trust. Use SDK documentation for implementation capabilities, not as a complete product reference. |
| Beli | [Product](https://beliapp.com/), [founder interview](https://www.founderbrew.com/stories/beli-founders-judy-thelen-eliot-frost-partnership-superpower), [reporting on user behavior](https://tastecooking.com/beli-invites-the-loneliest-generation-to-dine-out/) for community, trusted recommendations, local product value, adoption, and repeat use. |
| AllTrails | [Product](https://www.alltrails.com/), [Help Center](https://support.alltrails.com/hc/en-us) for local discovery, useful place information, community knowledge, and clear design. |
| TikTok | [Product help](https://support.tiktok.com/), [developer resources](https://developers.tiktok.com/), [ByteDance public repositories](https://github.com/bytedance). |
| Instagram | [Product help](https://help.instagram.com/), [Design at Meta](https://www.meta.com/design-at-meta/), [Meta Engineering](https://engineering.fb.com/), [public repositories](https://github.com/facebook). |
| Snapchat | [Engineering](https://eng.snap.com/), [product help](https://help.snapchat.com/), [public repositories](https://github.com/Snapchat). |
| Uber | [Engineering](https://www.uber.com/us/en/blog/engineering/), [Base Web design system](https://baseweb.design/), [public repositories](https://github.com/uber). |
| Lyft | [Engineering](https://eng.lyft.com/), [product help](https://help.lyft.com/), [public repositories](https://github.com/lyft). |
| Airbnb | [Engineering](https://airbnb.tech/), [product help](https://www.airbnb.com/help), [public repositories](https://github.com/airbnb). |
| Shopify | [Engineering](https://shopify.engineering/), [Polaris](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/polaris), [public repositories](https://github.com/Shopify). |
| Spotify | [Engineering](https://engineering.atspotify.com/), [product help](https://support.spotify.com/), [partner design guidelines](https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/design), [public repositories](https://github.com/spotify). |
| Facebook | [Product help](https://www.facebook.com/help/), [Design at Meta](https://www.meta.com/design-at-meta/), [Meta Engineering](https://engineering.fb.com/), [public repositories](https://github.com/facebook). |

A web component library, partner branding guide, or developer API isn't a complete consumer-app design specification. Use each source only for what it establishes. Discover further official design guidance through these publishers. Don't invent missing style guides.

Use the relevant listing and verify the publisher identity. Select images that show the interface being studied, not just promotional artwork. For other apps from the same company, follow the publisher's official links.

Apple's [public lookup service](https://itunes.apple.com/lookup?id=429047995&country=us) can provide store image URLs without browser automation. Inspect the returned images rather than inferring their content from metadata. For Google Play, use the public listing's images. If retrieval fails, use official demonstrations or supplied captures and state any remaining evidence gap.
